prompt: A hectare is the area of a square piece of land measuring 100 m by 100 m. Farmer Jabulani bought a 45 hectare farm for R180 000. The price in rands per square metre paid by farmer Jabulani was

solutions.title: Convert to square metres
solutions.body:
45 hectares is $45\times 100\times 100 = 450\,000$ m$^2$. The price per square metre is $\frac{180\,000}{450\,000}=\frac{2}{5}=0{,}4$ rands.

**Answer: (E)**

solutions.title: Per hectare first
solutions.body:
One hectare costs $180\,000/45=4000$ rands and has $10\,000$ m$^2$, so one m$^2$ costs $4000/10\,000=0{,}4$ rands.

**Answer: (E)**

prompt: The number halfway between $\frac18$ and $\frac1{10}$ is

solutions.title: Average
solutions.body:
The number halfway between two numbers is their average: $\frac12\left(\frac18+\frac1{10}\right)=\frac12\cdot\frac{5+4}{40}=\frac9{80}$.

**Answer: (E)**

solutions.title: Midpoint by distance
solutions.body:
The difference is $\frac18-\frac1{10}=\frac1{40}$; half of it is $\frac1{80}$, so the midpoint is $\frac1{10}+\frac1{80}=\frac9{80}$.

**Answer: (E)**

prompt: Which of the following numbers is the largest? (Remember $6{,}\overline{967}$ means $6{,}967967967\ldots$)

solutions.title: Write out the decimals
solutions.body:
(A) 3,14160000... (B) 3,14161416... (C) 3,1416416... (D) 3,14161616... (E) 3,14166666...

The first four decimal places are the same in all five (1416), but the fifth decimal place is 0, 1, 4, 1, 6 respectively. Hence (E) is largest.

Check (C): $3{,}1\overline{416}=3{,}1416416\ldots$ has fifth decimal 4, which is less than 6.

**Answer: (E)**

prompt: If $\dfrac xy=0{,}75$, then the value of $(x+2y)/x$ equals

solutions.title: Compute y/x
solutions.body:
$\frac xy=\frac34$, so $\frac yx=\frac43$. Then $\frac{x+2y}{x}=1+2\cdot\frac yx=1+\frac83=\frac{11}3$.

**Answer: (A)**

prompt: If $f(x)=2x-1$ and $g(x)=\frac1x$, then $f\left(g\left(-\frac12\right)\right)$ equals
If $p+q=4$ and $p^2-q^2=1$, then $p-q$ equals

solutions.title: Difference of squares
solutions.body:
$p^2-q^2=(p-q)(p+q)$, so $1=(p-q)\cdot4$ and $p-q=\frac14$.

**Answer: (E)**

prompt:
Ixopo General Dealer sells fish. This can be bought in three kinds of packets:

- A 400 g packet at R10,00 each
- A 500 g packet at R13,00 each
- A 800 g packet at R16,00 each.

You want to buy 2 kg of fish, which can be done in different ways. The difference, in rands, between the most expensive combination and the cheapest combination will be

solutions.title: List all combinations
solutions.body:
We need $400a+500b+800c=2000$, i.e. $4a+5b+8c=20$. Then $5b$ must be divisible by 4, so $b=0$ or $b=4$.

- $b=4$: $a=c=0$, cost $4\times13=52$.
- $b=0$: $a+2c=5$ gives $(a,c)=(5,0),(3,1),(1,2)$ with costs $50$, $46$, $42$.

The most expensive is R52 and the cheapest R42; the difference is R10.

**Answer: (A) 10**

solutions.title: Price per 100 g
solutions.body:
400 g: R2,50 per 100 g; 500 g: R2,60; 800 g: R2,00. Cheapest is to use as many 800 g packets as possible: two 800 g and one 400 g, R42. Dearest is only 500 g packets: $4\times 13=$ R52. Difference R10.

**Answer: (A) 10**

prompt: Telkom plans to install 732 000 new telephone lines in the year 2000. On average the new lines will be installed at the rate of approximately

solutions.title: Seconds per line
solutions.body:
The year 2000 has 366 days, i.e. $366\times24\times60\times60\approx 31.6$ million seconds. Dividing by $732\,000$ gives about $43$ seconds per line, closest to 45 seconds.

Quick check: $732\,000=2\times366\times1000$, so one line per $\frac{86400}{2000}=43{,}2$ seconds.

**Answer: (D)**

prompt: The average of three numbers is 18. If the largest number is replaced by the number 38, then the average of the three numbers is 23. The original number that was replaced, is

solutions.title: Compare the sums
solutions.body:
Original sum: $3\times18=54$. New sum: $3\times23=69$. The replacement raised the sum by 15, so the replaced number is $38-15=23$.

**Answer: (B) 23**

prompt: Two triangles, with given side lengths, are shown. To paint triangle A you need 4 ml of paint. The number of ml of paint needed for triangle B is

solutions.title: Similar triangles
solutions.body:
The sides of B are $3$ times those of A ($6,8,4\to18,24,12$), so the area of B is $3^2=9$ times the area of A. Paint needed: $9\times4=36$ ml.

**Answer: (D) 36**

prompt: A question paper consists of twenty questions. Section A (questions 1 to 5) are worth 3 marks each, Section B (questions 6 to 15) are worth 5 marks each and Section C (questions 16 to 20) are worth 7 marks each. Ellie scores 100% in section A, and 90% in section B. The least number of questions she should answer correctly in section C to score more than 80% overall is

solutions.title: Count marks
solutions.body:
Total marks: $5\cdot3+10\cdot5+5\cdot7=15+50+35=100$. Ellie gets $15+0{,}9\cdot50=60$ from sections A and B. She needs more than $80$, so more than $20$ from section C. With $k$ correct answers she gets $7k>20$, so $k\ge3$ ($7\cdot2=14$ is not enough, $7\cdot3=21$ is).

**Answer: (C) 3**

prompt: In the given figure, $ABD$ is an equilateral triangle. If the area of triangle $ABC$ is twice the area of triangle $ADC$, then the size of angle $BAC$ is equal to

solutions.title: Areas with a common height
solutions.body:
Triangles $ABC$ and $ADC$ have the same height from $A$, so their areas are in the ratio of the bases: $BC=2DC$. As $BD=BC-DC=DC$, we get $DC=BD=AD$ (equilateral), so triangle $ADC$ is isosceles with $AD=DC$. The exterior angle $\angle ADB=60^\circ$ equals $\angle DAC+\angle DCA=2\angle DAC$, so $\angle DAC=30^\circ$. Hence $\angle BAC=60^\circ+30^\circ=90^\circ$.

**Answer: (A) $90^\circ$**

solutions.title: Circle argument
solutions.body:
$D$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $DA=DB=DC$, so $A$ lies on the circle with diameter $BC$. By Thales, $\angle BAC=90^\circ$.

**Answer: (A)**

prompt: The horizontal and vertical distance between adjacent points of the grid shown, is one unit. The area of the triangle $ABC$ is

solutions.title: Surround with a right triangle
solutions.body:
Take coordinates with $A=(0,0)$, $B=(3,2)$, $C=(4,3)$. Drop perpendiculars to $E=(4,0)$ and $D=(3,0)$. Triangle $ACE$ has area $\frac12\cdot4\cdot3=6$; triangle $ABD$ has area $\frac12\cdot3\cdot2=3$; trapezium $BDEC$ has area $\frac12(2+3)\cdot1=\frac52$. So the area of $ABC$ is $6-3-\frac52=\frac12$.

**Answer: (B) 1/2**

solutions.title: Cross product
solutions.body:
With $\vec{AB}=(3,2)$ and $\vec{AC}=(4,3)$ the area is $\frac12|3\cdot3-2\cdot4|=\frac12$.

**Answer: (B)**

prompt: In a certain school there are two grade 11 classes with the same number of learners in each. The ratio of girls to boys in one class is $1:2$ and in the other class it is $3:2$. The ratio of girls to boys in the entire grade 11 is

solutions.title: Pick a class size
solutions.body:
Take 15 learners in each class. Class 1: 5 girls, 10 boys. Class 2: 9 girls, 6 boys. Total: 14 girls and 16 boys, ratio $14:16=7:8$.

**Answer: (C) 7:8**

prompt: In a science experiment, you are trying to separate sugar from a solution of water and sugar by heating and evaporating the water. The mass of the solution is 2 kg which contains 90% water and 10% sugar by mass. What will be the mass of the solution if after some time you find it to contain 85% water?

solutions.title: Sugar stays the same
solutions.body:
The sugar is $10\%$ of 2 kg $=0{,}2$ kg and does not change. When the solution is $85\%$ water it is $15\%$ sugar, so its mass $M$ satisfies $0{,}15M=0{,}2$, giving $M=\frac{0{,}2}{0{,}15}=\frac43=1{,}\overline3$ kg.

**Answer: (D)**

prompt: The sum of the digits of $10^{20}-2$ when expressed as a single number is

solutions.title: Write out the number
solutions.body:
$10^{20}-2=99\ldots98$ with nineteen 9s followed by an 8. Digit sum: $19\cdot9+8=179$.

**Answer: (E) 179**

prompt: Mr. and Mrs. Mahomole, working in shifts, made an agreement with their employer that Mr. Mahomole will be off every 8th day and Mrs. Mahomole every 5th day. If they were both off on Thursday the 20th of January 2000, on what date will they be off together the last time during year 2000?

solutions.title: Use the LCM
solutions.body:
They are both off every $\operatorname{lcm}(8,5)=40$ days. The year 2000 is a leap year with 366 days, so 31 December is $366-20=346$ days after 20 January. The largest multiple of 40 not exceeding 346 is 320, which is 26 days before 31 December: 31 - 26 = 5 December.

**Answer: (B) 5 December**

prompt: $ABC$ is a right-angled triangle with $D$, $E$ and $F$ the midpoints of the sides as indicated. If $CD=2$ then $AE^2+BF^2$ equals

solutions.title: Pythagoras three times
solutions.body:
The angle at $C$ is $90^\circ$ and $D$ is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, so $D$ is the circumcentre and $AB=2CD=4$. Then $AE^2=AC^2+CE^2=AC^2+\frac14BC^2$ and $BF^2=BC^2+CF^2=BC^2+\frac14AC^2$. Adding, $AE^2+BF^2=\frac54(AC^2+BC^2)=\frac54AB^2=\frac54\cdot16=20$.

**Answer: (D) 20**

prompt: When written in full $2^{2000}$ has $m$ digits and $5^{2000}$ has $n$ digits. The value of $m+n$ is

solutions.title: Leading digits
solutions.body:
Write $2^{2000}=a\cdot10^{m-1}$ and $5^{2000}=b\cdot10^{n-1}$ with $1\le a,b<10$ real. Since neither number is a power of $10$, $a,b>1$. Then $ab\cdot10^{m+n-2}=10^{2000}$, so $ab$ is a power of $10$ with $1<ab<100$, i.e. $ab=10$. Hence $10^{m+n-1}=10^{2000}$ and $m+n=2001$.

**Answer: (D) 2001**

solutions.title: Logarithms
solutions.body:
The number of digits of $N$ is $\lfloor\log_{10}N\rfloor+1$. With $x=2000\log_{10}2$ and $y=2000\log_{10}5$ we have $x+y=2000$, and neither is an integer (neither $2^{2000}$ nor $5^{2000}$ is a power of 10). So $\lfloor x\rfloor+\lfloor y\rfloor=1999$ and $m+n=1999+2=2001$.

**Answer: (D) 2001**
